o: The words Moses spake to Israel in the plains of Moab, The promise of Canaan.
Judges provided for the people.

bg: deuteronomy

In all the Hebrew manuscripts the Pentateuch (q.v.) forms one roll or volume divided into larger and smaller sections called parshioth_ and _sedarim. It is not easy to say when it was divided into five books.
Kadesh

Holy, or Kadesh-Barnea, sacred desert of wandering, a place on the south-eastern border of Palestine, about 165 miles from Horeb. It lay in the "wilderness" or "desert of Zin" (Gen. 14:7; Num. 13:3-26; 14:29-33; 20:1; 27:14), on the border of Edom (20:16). From this place, in compliance with the desire of the people, Moses sent forth "twelve spies" to spy the land.
Seir

The name of a mountainous region occupied by the Edomites, extending along the eastern side of the Arabah from the south-eastern extremity of the Dead Sea to near the Akabah, or the eastern branch of the Red Sea. It was originally occupied by the Horites (Gen. 14:6), who were afterwards driven out by the Edomites (Gen. 32:3; 33:14, 16).
Moses

Suddenly the angel of the Lord appeared to him in the burning bush (Ex. 3), and commissioned him to go down to Egypt and "bring forth the children of Israel" out of bondage. He was at first unwilling to go, but at length he was obedient to the heavenly vision, and left the land of Midian (4:18-26). On the way he was met by Aaron (q.v.) and the elders of Israel (27-31). He and Aaron had a hard task before them; but th

People named: Moses, Horeb, Sihon, Og, Edrei, On. Places: Kadesh, Jordan, Seir, Egypt, Paran.
ch.mh: Moses spake to the people all the Lord had given him in commandment.
q: Read verses 1–8 (The words Moses spake to Israel in the plains of Moab, The promise of Canaan). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 9–18 (Judges provided for the people), what do you learn about family and generations?

What does Moses’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of leadership and kingship in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of Deuteronomy?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.aq: We are not straitened in the power and goodness of God; why should we be straitened in our own faith and hope?
ch.a: Before a decision this week, pause and ask what this chapter would counsel.

bg: deuteronomy

In all the Hebrew manuscripts the Pentateuch (q.v.) forms one roll or volume divided into larger and smaller sections called parshioth_ and _sedarim. It is not easy to say when it was divided into five books.
Seir

The name of a mountainous region occupied by the Edomites, extending along the eastern side of the Arabah from the south-eastern extremity of the Dead Sea to near the Akabah, or the eastern branch of the Red Sea. It was originally occupied by the Horites (Gen. 14:6), who were afterwards driven out by the Edomites (Gen. 32:3; 33:14, 16).
Zered

Zared, luxuriance; willow bush, a brook or valley communicating with the Dead Sea near its southern extremity (Num. 21:12; Deut. 2:14). It is called the "brook of the willows" (Isa. 15:7) and the "river of the wilderness" (Amos 6:14).
Sihon

Striking down. The whole country on the east of Jordan, from the Arnon to the Jabbok, was possessed by the Amorites, whose king, Sihon, refused to permit the Israelites to pass through his territory, and put his army in array against them.
ch.s: This chapter covers: The Edomites to be spared (vv. 1–7); The Moabites and Ammonites to be spared (vv. 8–23); The Amorites to be destroyed (vv. 24–37). People named: Esau, Sihon, Ammon, Moab, Lot, Emims. Places: Seir, Ar, Zered, Heshbon, Arnon.
ch.mh: Only a short account of the long stay of Israel in the wilderness is given.

What does Esau’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?

ch.aq: Let us, by reflecting upon God's dealings with his people Israel, be led to meditate upon our years spent in vanity, through our transgressions.
ch.a: Let the seriousness of God's judgment move you to examine your ways and to pray for others.

o: The conquest of Og king of Bashan.
The land of Gilead and Bashan.
Moses encourages Joshua.
bg: deuteronomy

In all the Hebrew manuscripts the Pentateuch (q.v.) forms one roll or volume divided into larger and smaller sections called parshioth_ and _sedarim. It is not easy to say when it was divided into five books.
Bashan

Light soil, first mentioned in Gen. 14:5, where it is said that Chedorlaomer and his confederates "smote the Rephaim in Ashteroth," where Og the king of Bashan had his residence. At the time of Israel's entrance into the Promised Land, Og came out against them, but was utterly routed (Num. 21:33-35; Deut. 3:1-7).
Gilead
Hill of testimony, (Gen. 31:21), a mountainous region east of Jordan. From its mountainous character it is called "the mount of Gilead" (Gen. 31:25).
Og

Gigantic, the king of Bashan, who was defeated by Moses in a pitched battle at Edrei, and was slain along with his sons (Deut. 1:4), and whose kingdom was given to the tribes of Reuben and Gad and half the tribe of Manasseh (Num. 21:32-35; Deut. 3:1-13). His bedstead (or rather sarcophagus) was of iron (or ironstone), 9 cubits in length and 4 cubits in breadth.
ch.s: This chapter covers: The conquest of Og king of Bashan (vv. 1–11); The land of Gilead and Bashan (vv. 12–20); Moses encourages Joshua (vv. 21–29). People named: Og, Edrei, Sihon, Ammon, Manasseh, Joshua. Places: Bashan, Jordan, Gilead, Argob, Arnon.
ch.mh: Og was very powerful, but he did not take warning by the ruin of Sihon, and desire conditions of peace.
q: Read verses 1–11 (The conquest of Og king of Bashan). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 12–20 (The land of Gilead and Bashan), what do you learn about leadership and kingship?

What does Og’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of the kingdom of god in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of Deuteronomy?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.aq: And if we have the earnest and prospect of heaven, let these suffice us; let us submit to the Lord's will, and speak no more to Him of matters which he sees good to refuse us.
ch.a: Set aside a specific time this week to pray through this chapter's key verse.

Burning, a place in the wilderness of Paran, where the "fire of the Lord" consumed the murmuring Israelites (Num. 11:3; Deut. 9:22). It was also called Kibroth-hattaavah (q.v.).
Jacob

When Isaac was about 160 years of age, Jacob and his mother conspired to deceive the aged patriarch (Gen. 27), with the view of procuring the transfer of the birthright to himself. bg: deuteronomy

In all the Hebrew manuscripts the Pentateuch (q.v.) forms one roll or volume divided into larger and smaller sections called parshioth_ and _sedarim. It is not easy to say when it was divided into five books.
Beeroth
Wells, one of the four cities of the Hivites which entered by fraud into a league with Joshua. It belonged to Benjamin (Josh. 18:25).
Aaron

Aaron was implicated in the sin of his brother at Meribah (Num. 20:8-13), and on that account was not permitted to enter the Promised Land. When the tribes arrived at Mount Hor, "in the edge of the land of Edom," at the command of God Moses led Aaron and his son Eleazar to the top of that mountain, in the sight of all the people.

Dathan

Welled; belonging to a fountain, a son of Eliab, a Reubenite, who joined Korah (q.v.) in his conspiracy, and with his accomplices was swallowed up by an earthquake (Num. 16:1; 26:9; Deut. 11:6; Ps. 106:17).

At the time of Israel's entrance into the Promised Land, Og came out against them, but was utterly routed (Num. 21:33-35; Deut. 3:1-7).
Sodom

Burning; the walled, a city in the vale of Siddim (Gen. 13:10; 14:1-16). The wickedness of its inhabitants brought down upon it fire from heaven, by which it was destroyed (18:16-33; 19:1-29; Deut. 23:17).
Gomorrah

Submersion, one of the five cities of the plain of Siddim (q.v.) which were destroyed by fire (Gen. 10:19; 13:10; 19:24, 28). These cities probably stood close together, and were near the northern extremity of what is now the Dead Sea.
ch.s: This chapter covers: The song of Moses (vv. 1,2); The character of God, The character of Israel (vv. 3–6); The great things God had done for Israel (vv. 7–14); The wickedness of Israel (vv. 19–25); The judgments which would come upon them for their sins (vv. 15–18); Deserved vengeance withheld (vv. 26–38); God's deliverance for his people (vv. 39–43); The exhortation with which the song was delivered (vv. 44–47); Moses to go up mount Nebo to die (vv. 48–52). People named: Moses, Adam, Jacob, Nun, Nebo, Moab. Places: Bashan, Sodom, Gomorrah, Jordan, Abarim.
ch.mh: Moses begins with a solemn appeal to heaven and earth, concerning the truth and importance of what he was about to say.

o: The glorious majesty of God.
The blessings of the twelve tribes.
Strength to believers.
The excellency of Israel.
bg: deuteronomy

In all the Hebrew manuscripts the Pentateuch (q.v.) forms one roll or volume divided into larger and smaller sections called parshioth_ and _sedarim. It is not easy to say when it was divided into five books.
Sinai
Of Sin (the moon god), called also Horeb, the name of the mountain district which was reached by the Hebrews in the third month after the Exodus. Here they remained encamped for about a whole year.
Jacob

When Isaac was about 160 years of age, Jacob and his mother conspired to deceive the aged patriarch (Gen. 27), with the view of procuring the transfer of the birthright to himself. The birthright secured to him who possessed it (1) superior rank in his family (Gen. 49:3); (2) a double portion of the paternal inheritance (Deut. 21:17); (3) the priestly office in the family (Num. 8:17-19); and (4) the promise of the Se
Moses
Thus died "Moses the man of God" (Deut. 33:1; Josh. 14:6). He was distinguished for his meekness and patience and firmness, and "he endured as seeing him who is invisible."
ch.s: This chapter covers: The glorious majesty of God (vv. 1–5); The blessings of the twelve tribes (vv. 6–23); Strength to believers (vv. 24,25); The excellency of Israel (vv. 26–29). People named: Jacob, Moses, Joseph, Zebulun, Gad, Naphtali. Places: Judah, Dan, Sinai, Seir, Paran.
ch.mh: To all his precepts, warnings, and prophecies, Moses added a solemn blessing.

o: Moses views the promised land from mount Nebo.

bg: deuteronomy

In all the Hebrew manuscripts the Pentateuch (q.v.) forms one roll or volume divided into larger and smaller sections called parshioth_ and _sedarim. It is not easy to say when it was divided into five books.
Jericho
This city was taken in a very remarkable manner by the Israelites (Josh. 6). God gave it into their hands.
Pisgah

A part, a mountain summit in the land of Moab, in the territory of Reuben, where Balak offered up sacrifices (Num. 21:20; 23:14), and from which Moses viewed the promised land (Deut. 3:27). It is probably the modern Jebel Siaghah.
Gilead
Hill of testimony, (Gen. 31:21), a mountainous region east of Jordan. From its mountainous character it is called "the mount of Gilead" (Gen. 31:25).
ch.s: This chapter covers: Moses views the promised land from mount Nebo (vv. 1–4); The death and burial of Moses, The mourning of the people (vv. 5–8); Joshua succeeds Moses, The praise of Moses (vv. 9–12). People named: Moses, Moab, Nebo, Naphtali, Ephraim, Manasseh. Places: Jericho, Pisgah, Gilead, Dan, Judah.
ch.mh: Moses seemed unwilling to leave his work; but that being finished, he manifested no unwillingness to die.
q: Read verses 1–4 (Moses views the promised land from mount Nebo). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
